title: Judges Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 13.

questions.question: Who did the LORD deliver the children of Israel into the hand of for forty years?
questions.correctAnswer: The Philistines
questions.explanation: Judges 13:1 states that the LORD delivered Israel into the hand of the Philistines for forty years.

questions.question: What was the name of the man from Zorah?
questions.correctAnswer: Manoah
questions.explanation: Judges 13:2 identifies the man from Zorah as Manoah.

questions.question: True or False: Manoah's wife was able to have children before the angel appeared to her.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 13:2 states that Manoah's wife was barren and bare not before the angel appeared to her.

questions.question: Who appeared to Manoah's wife to announce she would bear a son?
questions.correctAnswer: The angel of the LORD
questions.explanation: Judges 13:3 says the angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and announced she would bear a son.

questions.question: What was the woman instructed not to drink?
questions.correctAnswer: Wine nor strong drink
questions.explanation: Judges 13:4 commands the woman to not drink wine nor strong drink.

questions.question: True or False: The child to be born was to have a razor come upon his head.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 13:5 clearly states no razor shall come on the child's head because he shall be a Nazarite unto God.

questions.question: What special status was the child to have from the womb?
questions.correctAnswer: Nazarite
questions.explanation: Judges 13:5 states the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the child to be born, according to the angel?
options: To begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines
To lead the people into battle against Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: To begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines
questions.explanation: Judges 13:5 says the child shall begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines.

questions.question: What did Manoah's wife say about the man who appeared to her?
options: His countenance was like the countenance of an angel of God, very terrible
He was a familiar man from their village
He was a prophet of Baal
questions.correctAnswer: His countenance was like the countenance of an angel of God, very terrible
questions.explanation: Judges 13:6 describes the man of God’s countenance as like an angel of God, very terrible.

questions.question: True or False: The woman asked the angel where he was from and his name.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 13:6 states the woman did not ask the angel where he was from, nor did he tell her his name.

questions.question: What did the angel repeat to the woman in Judges 13:7?
options: To drink no wine nor strong drink and eat no unclean thing
questions.correctAnswer: To drink no wine nor strong drink and eat no unclean thing
questions.explanation: Judges 13:7 repeats the commands about drinking no wine or strong drink and eating no unclean thing.

questions.question: Who prayed for the angel of the LORD to come again and teach them what to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Manoah
questions.explanation: Judges 13:8 tells that Manoah intreated the LORD to send the man of God again to teach them what to do.

questions.question: True or False: God listened to Manoah's prayer and sent the angel again to the woman while she was alone.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 13:9 confirms God hearkened to Manoah’s voice and the angel appeared again to the woman while she was in the field alone.

questions.question: What did the woman do when the angel appeared to her the second time?
options: She ran and told her husband
questions.correctAnswer: She ran and told her husband
questions.explanation: Judges 13:10 says the woman made haste, ran, and showed her husband the angel’s appearance.

questions.question: In which order did these events occur in Judges 13:3-5? 1) The angel commands not to drink wine or strong drink, 2) The angel appears to the woman, 3) The angel says the child will be a Nazarite.
questions.explanation: Judges 13:3 shows the angel appearing first; 13:4 commands avoiding wine and unclean food; 13:5 describes the child as a Nazarite.

medium.title: Judges Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Manoah ask the man of God when he came again to them?
options: If he would stay for a meal
If he would teach them how to raise the child
questions.correctAnswer: If he would teach them how to raise the child
questions.explanation: Manoah asked the man of God to come again to teach them how to raise the child as recorded in Judges 13:8 and 13:11-12. This shows Manoah's desire for guidance in obedience to God's instructions.

questions.question: According to the angel's instructions, what was the woman not allowed to consume?
options: Anything from the vine, wine, strong drink, and unclean food
questions.correctAnswer: Anything from the vine, wine, strong drink, and unclean food
questions.explanation: The angel instructed that the woman must not eat anything from the vine nor drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing, as stated in Judges 13:4 and reinforced in 13:14.

questions.question: What was the angel of the LORD's response when Manoah asked if they could detain him for a meal?
options: He agreed to eat the meal
He refused to eat and said any offering must be to the LORD
He said he was too tired
He asked them to bring more offerings
questions.correctAnswer: He refused to eat and said any offering must be to the LORD
questions.explanation: In Judges 13:15-16, the angel refused to eat the bread and instructed that any burnt offering must be made to the LORD, emphasizing reverence and obedience.

questions.question: Why did the angel of the LORD say Manoah should not ask for his name?
options: Because his name was too long
Because he did not have a name
questions.correctAnswer: Because it was a secret
questions.explanation: The angel told Manoah that his name was secret, as recorded in Judges 13:18, highlighting the mystery and holiness of God's messenger.

questions.question: What did Manoah and his wife do when the angel ascended in the flame of the altar?
options: They fell on their faces to the ground
questions.correctAnswer: They fell on their faces to the ground
questions.explanation: Judges 13:20 states that Manoah and his wife fell on their faces to the ground upon witnessing the angel ascend in the flame, showing reverence and awe.

questions.question: What did Manoah conclude after the angel of the LORD no longer appeared to them?
options: That they had seen God and would surely die
That the angel was a prophet
That the child would be strong
questions.correctAnswer: That they had seen God and would surely die
questions.explanation: Manoah said to his wife, “We shall surely die, because we have seen God,” as recorded in Judges 13:22, reflecting the belief that seeing God’s presence brings death.

questions.question: How did Manoah's wife respond to his fear that they would die after seeing God?
options: She said God would punish them
She said God would not have accepted their offerings if He planned to kill them
questions.correctAnswer: She said God would not have accepted their offerings if He planned to kill them
questions.explanation: In Judges 13:23, she reassured Manoah that God would not have accepted their sacrifices or revealed these things if He intended to kill them, teaching trust in God's mercy.

questions.question: What does Judges 13:14 say will happen if the woman obeys the angel's command to avoid wine, strong drink, and unclean food?
options: She will bear a son who is a Nazarite to God
She will live a long life
questions.correctAnswer: She will bear a son who is a Nazarite to God
questions.explanation: Judges 13:14 instructs strict obedience to avoid certain things, continuing the promise in 13:5 that the son will be a Nazarite dedicated to God from birth, showing the link between obedience and God's plan.

questions.question: How does the passage from Judges 13:13-14 teach about obedience in Christian living?
options: Obedience to God's commands leads to blessings and fulfilling His purposes
Obedience is optional if we have faith
Obedience requires sacrifice but no reward
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's commands leads to blessings and fulfilling His purposes
questions.explanation: The angel's command to strictly observe instructions (Judges 13:13-14) shows that obedience is essential for God’s promise—here, the birth of a Nazarite son who will deliver Israel—to be realized, teaching the principle of faithful obedience.

questions.question: What does Judges 13:17-18 reveal about the nature of God's messengers?
options: Their names are always known to humans
Their identity is sometimes mysterious and secret
questions.correctAnswer: Their identity is sometimes mysterious and secret
questions.explanation: When Manoah asks the angel's name, the angel says it is secret (13:18), indicating that God’s messengers can be mysterious, reminding believers to trust God even without full understanding.

questions.question: In the context of Judges 13:10-13, what does the woman's haste to inform Manoah teach about faith and obedience?
options: Faith requires immediate sharing and seeking guidance
Faith is personal and should not be shared
questions.correctAnswer: Faith requires immediate sharing and seeking guidance
questions.explanation: The woman quickly runs to tell Manoah about the angel (13:10), and they seek further instruction (13:12-13), illustrating that faith involves sharing God’s messages and pursuing obedience together.

questions.question: True or False: Manoah immediately recognized the angel of the LORD as a divine messenger when he first spoke to him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 13:16 and 13:21 show Manoah did not recognize the angel as a divine being at first; it was only after the angel ascended in the flame that he knew the truth.

questions.question: True or False: The angel of the LORD accepted Manoah's invitation to stay and eat with them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: According to Judges 13:16, the angel refused to eat their bread and instructed that any offering must be made to the LORD, showing His distinct role as a heavenly messenger.

questions.question: True or False: The Spirit of the LORD began to move Samson in the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol after his birth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 13:25 states that the Spirit of the LORD began to move Samson at times in the camp of Dan, showing God's empowerment of Samson from an early age.

questions.question: What biblical truth about prayer and God’s responsiveness can be drawn from Manoah’s interaction with God in Judges 13:8-9?
options: God does not respond to human requests
God listens and responds to sincere prayers
Only priests can have their prayers answered
questions.correctAnswer: God listens and responds to sincere prayers
questions.explanation: Manoah prayed for the man of God to return (13:8), and God listened, sending the angel again (13:9), teaching that God attentively hears and answers sincere prayer.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 13.

questions.question: What offering did Manoah present to the LORD upon the rock?
options: A kid with a meat offering
questions.correctAnswer: A kid with a meat offering
questions.explanation: Judges 13:19 states that Manoah took a kid with a meat offering and offered it upon a rock unto the LORD.

questions.question: What miraculous event occurred as the flame went up from the altar?
options: The angel of the LORD ascended in the flame
questions.correctAnswer: The angel of the LORD ascended in the flame
questions.explanation: Judges 13:20 describes how the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame of the altar after the flame went up toward heaven.

questions.question: After the appearance of the angel, what was Manoah's initial reaction?
options: We shall surely die, because we have seen God
questions.correctAnswer: We shall surely die, because we have seen God
questions.explanation: Judges 13:22 records Manoah saying that they would surely die because they had seen God, showing his reverence and fear.

questions.question: What reasoning did Manoah's wife give to counter her husband's fear of death?
options: The LORD would not have accepted their offerings if He intended to kill them
God is merciful and will forgive them
They can atone by sacrifices later
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD would not have accepted their offerings if He intended to kill them
questions.explanation: Judges 13:23 shows Manoah’s wife explaining that if God intended to kill them, He would not have accepted their burnt and meat offerings nor revealed such things.

questions.question: What name was given to the son born to Manoah's wife?
questions.correctAnswer: Samson
questions.explanation: Judges 13:24 states that the woman bore a son and called his name Samson.

questions.question: Where did the Spirit of the LORD begin to move Samson at times?
options: In the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol
questions.correctAnswer: In the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol
questions.explanation: Judges 13:25 specifies that the Spirit of the LORD moved Samson at times in the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol.

questions.question: What was Manoah's request when he first spoke to the angel of the LORD?
options: That the angel return and teach how to raise the child
That the angel perform a miracle immediately
That the angel bless the land
That the angel defeat the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: That the angel return and teach how to raise the child
questions.explanation: Judges 13:8 shows Manoah praying to the LORD to send the man of God again to instruct them how to care for the child.

questions.question: What specific Nazarite restrictions did the angel command Manoah's wife to observe for the child?
options: No wine, strong drink, or unclean food
questions.correctAnswer: No wine, strong drink, or unclean food
questions.explanation: Judges 13:14 commands the woman to avoid anything from the vine, wine, strong drink, and unclean food for the child.

questions.question: What is the significance of the angel of the LORD not eating the bread offered by Manoah?
options: To indicate he was a divine messenger, not a human
To show rejection of the offering
questions.correctAnswer: To indicate he was a divine messenger, not a human
questions.explanation: Judges 13:16 reveals the angel declined eating, indicating his heavenly nature and instructing that offerings be made to the LORD instead.

questions.question: How does the angel of the LORD respond when Manoah asks his name?
options: He says the name is secret
questions.correctAnswer: He says the name is secret
questions.explanation: Judges 13:18 shows the angel replying that his name is secret, emphasizing the mystery of divine revelation.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage also describes an angel announcing the birth of a significant child to a barren woman?
options: Luke 1:11-20 (Angel announcing John the Baptist's birth)
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 1:11-20 (Angel announcing John the Baptist's birth)
questions.explanation: Luke 1:11-20 parallels Judges 13, where an angel announces the birth of a child to a barren woman, highlighting a thematic connection of divine intervention in childbirth.

questions.question: The narrative of Samson’s birth in Judges 13 is an example of which literary device common in biblical birth narratives?
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: This chapter uses typology by foreshadowing Samson as a deliverer, similar to other biblical heroes born under divine intervention, marking a pattern seen in Scripture.

questions.question: The term 'Nazarite' in the context of Samson’s birth means which of the following?
options: One separated or consecrated to God
questions.correctAnswer: One separated or consecrated to God
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Nazarite' (Nazir) means separated or consecrated to God, as indicated in Judges 13:5 where Samson is dedicated from the womb.

questions.question: How does the chapter portray Manoah’s understanding of the angel's true identity before and after the altar event?
options: He did not know initially but recognized him as an angel after the flame ascended
He always knew the angel’s identity
He thought the angel was a man of war
questions.correctAnswer: He did not know initially but recognized him as an angel after the flame ascended
questions.explanation: Judges 13:16 and 13:21 indicate Manoah did not know the angel’s identity at first, but after witnessing the flame ascend, he realized the visitor was the angel of the LORD.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God’s Spirit moving upon a chosen individual as seen in Samson’s story?
options: Acts 10:38 (God anointed Jesus with the Holy Ghost)
questions.correctAnswer: Acts 10:38 (God anointed Jesus with the Holy Ghost)
questions.explanation: Acts 10:38 parallels Judges 13:25 by describing God anointing Jesus with the Holy Ghost, highlighting the Spirit’s empowering presence on chosen individuals.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is taught by the fact that the angel of the LORD appeared to Manoah's wife and gave specific instructions about her pregnancy?
options: God sovereignly initiates salvation history through miraculous births
Human effort alone secures deliverance from enemies
The angel's appearance was merely symbolic with no real intervention
Manoah's family was responsible for their own salvation
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly initiates salvation history through miraculous births
questions.explanation: Judges 13:3-5 shows the angel of the LORD announcing a miraculous birth and giving Nazarite instructions, demonstrating God's sovereign intervention in salvation history. This aligns with divine sovereignty in salvation as in Isaiah 9:6 and Luke 1:35.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is primarily demonstrated when He hearkens to Manoah’s prayer and sends the angel again?
questions.correctAnswer: Immanence
questions.explanation: Judges 13:8-9 shows God responding directly to Manoah’s prayer by sending the angel again, revealing God’s immanence—His nearness and active involvement in human affairs (Psalm 145:18).

questions.question: What theological significance does the Nazarite vow in this chapter convey about Samson’s role?
options: Separation unto God for divine purpose
A symbol of Israel’s political independence
A ritual cleansing for priests only
A sign of wealth and social status
questions.correctAnswer: Separation unto God for divine purpose
questions.explanation: Judges 13:5-7 highlights the Nazarite vow, showing Samson’s consecration from the womb, symbolizing separation unto God for a divine mission, consistent with Numbers 6:1-21.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Judges 13 contribute to the broader redemptive story of Scripture?
options: It foreshadows Christ as the deliverer from oppression
It introduces the Mosaic Law for the first time
It explains the origin of the Davidic monarchy
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ as the deliverer from oppression
questions.explanation: Judges 13:5 and 24-25 show Samson as a deliverer raising deliverance from Philistine oppression, foreshadowing Christ’s ultimate redemption (Acts 13:23).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Judges 13:4 and 13:14 provide about sanctification?
options: Sanctification involves obedience to God’s commands from conception onward
Sanctification is only ceremonial without moral implications
Sanctification is a communal act unrelated to personal conduct
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves obedience to God’s commands from conception onward
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 14 repeatedly command abstaining from wine and unclean things, showing sanctification as holy living initiated even before birth, consistent with 1 Thessalonians 4:3-4.

questions.question: How does the angel of the LORD’s refusal to eat Manoah’s bread in Judges 13:16 reveal a divine attribute?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and self-sufficiency
questions.explanation: Judges 13:16 shows the angel refusing human hospitality, emphasizing God’s holiness and that He is not dependent on human provisions, reflecting divine self-sufficiency (Exodus 3:2-6).

questions.question: What does the response of Manoah and his wife upon seeing the angel ascend in the flame indicate about their understanding of divine holiness?
options: They recognize God’s overwhelming holiness and fear
They believe the angel is a mere human
questions.correctAnswer: They recognize God’s overwhelming holiness and fear
questions.explanation: Judges 13:20-22 shows them falling on their faces and fearing death, indicating awe and recognition of divine holiness (Isaiah 6:5).

questions.question: What is the apologetic response to sceptics who claim that the miraculous birth narrative in Judges 13 is mythological rather than historical?
options: Judges 13:3-24 presents detailed historical and theological elements consistent with divine intervention, not myth
The text admits it is a myth
It is purely allegorical with no real birth
It contradicts all other biblical miracles
questions.correctAnswer: Judges 13:3-24 presents detailed historical and theological elements consistent with divine intervention, not myth
questions.explanation: The chapter gives precise names, places, and instructions (verses 2-24), affirming its historicity and theological purpose, consistent with other biblical miracles like Jesus’ birth (Luke 1).

questions.question: How does the dialogue between Manoah and the angel (Judges 13:17-18) reveal God's transcendence and mystery?
options: God’s name is secret, highlighting divine mystery beyond human comprehension
God reveals His name fully to Manoah
God is easily understood by humans
questions.correctAnswer: God’s name is secret, highlighting divine mystery beyond human comprehension
questions.explanation: Verse 18 shows the angel declines to disclose his name, illustrating God's transcendence and inscrutability (Isaiah 55:8-9).

questions.question: What does the birth of Samson and the Spirit of the LORD moving him at times (Judges 13:24-25) teach about the doctrine of the Spirit's role in salvation history?
options: The Spirit empowers chosen individuals for God’s purposes
The Spirit is unrelated to human activity
The Spirit acts only after death
The Spirit is a created force
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit empowers chosen individuals for God’s purposes
questions.explanation: Verses 24-25 indicate the Spirit’s active empowerment for deliverance, consistent with the Spirit’s role in the Old and New Testaments (Isaiah 61:1, Acts 1:8).

questions.question: What combined teaching about human sin and divine judgment is drawn from Judges 13:1 and 13:5?
options: Israel’s sin resulted in Philistine oppression, but God raises a deliverer to save His people
Israel’s sin was ignored by God
Philistine rule was due to Israel’s military weakness alone
questions.correctAnswer: Israel’s sin resulted in Philistine oppression, but God raises a deliverer to save His people
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows Israel’s evil and punishment, and verse 5 shows God’s plan to deliver via Samson, illustrating divine justice and mercy (Romans 11:26).

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by Manoah’s fear that they would die because they saw God (Judges 13:22) and his wife’s reassurance (Judges 13:23)?
options: The doctrine of God’s holiness and graciousness
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God’s holiness and graciousness
questions.explanation: Their dialogue shows reverence for God's holiness (fear of death) balanced with trust in His grace (accepting offerings), reflecting God’s holy yet merciful nature (Exodus 33:20, Psalm 103:8).

questions.question: How does the description of Samson’s upbringing in Judges 13:25 highlight the theme of divine blessing despite human brokenness?
options: The Spirit’s movement shows God’s blessing even in a rebellious era
Samson’s strength was natural and unrelated to God
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit’s movement shows God’s blessing even in a rebellious era
questions.explanation: Verse 25 records God’s Spirit moving Samson amidst Israel’s sin, illustrating God’s mercy and blessing despite human sinfulness (Psalm 78:38-39).

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by comparing the instructions given to Manoah’s wife with the idea that Samson was set apart from the womb?
options: Sanctification and divine calling begin before birth
Divine calling happens only after maturity
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification and divine calling begin before birth
questions.explanation: Judges 13:4-5 and 7 emphasize the Nazarite vow from the womb, teaching that God’s calling and sanctification can be prenatal, consistent with Jeremiah 1:5.

questions.question: What does the offering of a burnt offering and a meat offering upon a rock in Judges 13:19 reveal about Old Testament worship and God's acceptance?
options: God accepts sincere sacrifice regardless of location
Sacrifice must be done only at the temple
God rejects all offerings outside Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: God accepts sincere sacrifice regardless of location
questions.explanation: Verse 19 shows sacrifice on a rock, indicating God’s acceptance is based on heart sincerity, not just location, paralleling Samuel’s narrative (1 Samuel 7:9).
